subject: general
question:
The sum of the zeros of the polynomial

5x² + (5p – 1)x – (2p + 5) is the same as one fourth of their product. Find the value of p.
solution:
**Given:**

Sum of the zeros of the polynomial 5x2 + (5p – 1)x – (2p + 5) = 1/4 × Product of zeros 

**Formulas used:**

Standard form of polynomial, ax² + bx + c = 0

Sum of the zeros = - b/a 

Product of the zeros = c/a 

**Calculation:**

Sum of the zeros = - (5p - 1)/5 

Product of zeros = - (2p + 5)/5 

As per the question;

⇒ - (5p - 1)/5 = 1/4 × [- (2p + 5)/5]

⇒ (5p - 1) = (2p + 5)/4 

⇒ 20p - 4 = 2p + 5 

⇒ 20p - 2p = 5 + 4 

⇒ 18p = 9 

⇒ p = 9/18 = 1/2 

**∴ The value of p = 1/2 **
